messages:
zoe (Docs): Opening a tiny PR to tighten SOC2 wording on audit logs and add a short Node SDK snippet + retention API example. Need quick legal + security sanity check before merge.

pat (Security): Quick asks: 1) use 'recommended' for retention numbers unless contractually guaranteed; 2) mention append-only storage + integrity checks; 3) call out PII redaction options.

morgan (Legal): Agreed. Also say retention may be extended for legal or regulatory obligations and that customer agreements can override defaults. Avoid hard guarantees.

zoe (Docs): Draft copy I'll add: "Audit logs: Redwood retains audit logs to support security investigations, compliance, and contractual obligations. Recommended retention: 90 days (dev), 24 months (prod). Actual retention is configurable and may be extended to meet legal or contractual requirements. For private deployments, customers can control retention via the console or retention API. Sensitive fields can be redacted before long-term storage; see the data redaction guide."

sam (DevEx): Small nit: use "Redwood retains" for consistency. Also include this Node snippet for audit correlation headers:
```js
// attach audit metadata for traceability
await client.generate({
  model: 'rw-instruct-1',
  input: 'Summarize this document',
  headers: { 'x-redwood-audit-id': 'acct-555-evt-2026' }
});
```

zoe (Docs): Adding a retention API example for Dedicated/Private customers per infra request:
```json
{ "policy_name": "prod-default", "retention_days": 730, "redaction": { "pii_fields": ["email", "phone"], "method": "mask" } }
```

pat (Security): Also please add: "Audit logs are stored in append-only storage with integrity monitoring; deletions are logged and require authorization." That helps during SOC2 reviews.

morgan (Legal): +1. If we keep numbers, label them 'recommended' and coordinate with sales for any SLA commitments.

infra-bot: docs CI: \u2705, staging build: \u2705

zoe (Docs): Thanks all. I'll update the PR with these edits, fix the redaction link (anchor differs), and merge after legal sign-off.
